body.title: Retirement what-if
body.detail: Type your own numbers and Jarvis plays out 10,000 made-up futures. The answer is a range, never one exact figure. It stays on screen only: never read aloud, never remembered, never sent to a web search or a chatbot, and not saved.

fields.label: Age you stop working
fields.help: A whole number. If you already have, type your age now.

fields.label: Plan the money to age
fields.help: How long the money should last. Must be after the age you stop working.

fields.label: Savings you have now
fields.help: In today's money. Type 0 if none.

fields.label: You add each year until you stop working
fields.help: In today's money. Type 0 if none.

fields.label: You spend each year in retirement
Pension or other income each year (optional)
fields.help: In today's money. It only ever covers spending; extra is not saved.

fields.label: That income starts at age (optional)
fields.help: Leave empty to start when you stop working.

fields.help: A placeholder, not advice. Change it.

fields.help: A placeholder, not advice. Change it.

fields.help: A placeholder, not advice. Change it.

summary: In about 71 of 100 simulated futures your money lasts to age 95. Where it runs out, that is usually at about age 81 to 89.
If yearly returns are 1 point lower, that becomes about 51 of 100; 1 point higher, about 86 of 100.
In a poor case (1 in 10) the money runs out at about age 82.
The middle case leaves about 560,000 at age 95; a good case (1 in 10) about 3,500,000.
